prompt:
Render exactly TWO isolated orthographic REAR views in one transparent 1-column x 2-row atlas. Row1 is Personal Space warm wood plank stairs UP; row2 is the matching stairs DOWN. The target source-pair reference gives those row identities and the exact warm orange-brown timber, dark outline, rail thickness, and step count. The second reference is an accepted generated underside only for wood material and frame style, not for camera.

This camera is level and looks straight at the CLOSED REAR SUPPORT END of the staircase, from the opposite end of the run. It must NOT show the upper tread tops, a stair cavity, a plan view, or the front stairwell. Draw an upright solid wood rear riser/support face spanning the full stair width and the same full vertical Z height as the accepted FRONT/side views; two side rail posts frame it, with only narrow tread/riser edges or support rails visible behind the solid panel. Use one continuous dark warm-wood backing panel with plausible horizontal seams that follow the stair count, matching the source stair rails. For UP vs DOWN, follow the source row's rise orientation; the reverse support is the opposite end, not a duplicate front.

One complete object per row, centered with clear transparent margin, no clipping. Crisp pixel-art; no perspective/isometric, no text, labels, or background. Hidden reverse structure is inferred conservatively.
